_readme:
The residential register — what each building or agency STATES about itself, in its own words, with the source and the date somebody read it. Same discipline as data/curated/beauty.json and elephants.json: a row is the venue's own claim, never the ants' opinion; 'unstated' means the pages read did not say — it is not a no. Nothing here ranks a building, prices a neighbourhood, or calls anywhere good for anyone: this register holds what is posted, dated, and nothing else.

WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. OpenStreetMap holds 322 residential records across both provinces and knows almost nothing a renter asks at the desk: 77 state their floor count, 41 a phone, 14 a website — and not one records the per-unit electric rate, the deposit, whether the furniture comes with the room, or whether a dog may. audit_realestate.py proved the other half: across all 19,977 records, ZERO names say furnished and ZERO post a rate. Every question that decides whether a person takes the room is answered by the building stating it, an owner ticking their own facets, or a person at the desk — never by a crawl. The same is true of the one number a farang condo buyer asks first (what is left of the foreign quota): it lives at the juristic office and changes with every transfer, so a row may carry it ONLY as a dated statement from the building's own channel, and the date is the claim.

Fields per row: `place` (record id), `name`, `stated` (facet key -> yes | unstated, exactly the keys in the `realestate` set of data/facets.json), `rents_th`/`rents_en` as posted (the spread, never a welded average — the make_shelf_cards lesson), `rates_th`/`rates_en` (per-unit water and electric as posted), `note_th`/`note_en`, `source`, `fetched`, `stated_by`. Agencies use the same shape; their `stated` rows simply draw on the generic keys (english, lineId is a claim field, not a facet).
_doors: Nothing in `buildings` yet, and that is the true state, not an oversight — no building's own page has been read, because reading them is network work and WO-27's build was zero-network. The queue is ready: 12 residential records carry a first-hand website of their own (Airport Home Condominium, Life in Town, วีระชัยคอร์ต, Ping View, Smith Suites, the two Hinokï towers, Nimman and Me, The Mirror, Chiang Mai Riverside Condominium, The Empire Residence, The Iris Chotana), and they are the first 12 reads the moment Nan says go. See notes/realestate-proposal-2026-08-21.md for the numbered doors.
